metadata.title: User Guide for the TIMSS International Database: Primary and Middle School Years (Population 1 and Population 2) Data Collected in 1995

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This TIMSS user guide documents a two-stage stratified cluster sampling design for Population 1 and Population 2, with schools sampled first and classrooms sampled within schools (and an optional third stage sampling students within classrooms). It explains that analyses requiring population estimates should use the provided sampling weights that account for selection probabilities, stratification/disproportional sampling, and non-response adjustments. The guide also provides multiple student weight variants (e.g., TOTWGT for common mean/proportion estimation; SENWGT for equal country contribution; HOUWGT for using sample-size-based significance testing) and describes jackknife repeated replication (JRR) replicate weights for sampling variance estimation. Because this document is a database user guide rather than an empirical study estimating model parameters, it does not specify whether any particular analyst should apply weights in a specific ML pipeline; instead, it instructs users to apply the appropriate weight variables and JRR zones when computing standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a technical user guide describing how TIMSS achievement scores and plausible values are constructed and how to use the TIMSS International Database. It does not present a student-level predictive analysis with a defined dependent variable and therefore does not report a missing-data handling strategy for an empirical model. Missingness is discussed indirectly through sampling exclusions and the plausible-values framework, but no explicit imputation/deletion rule for an analysis dataset is provided in the guide.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The guide defines TIMSS Population 1 and Population 2 target populations as students in two adjacent grades with the largest proportions of 9-year-olds and 13-year-olds, respectively, and describes that national research coordinators operationally define national desired populations (potentially excluding remote regions or segments of the educational system). It specifies a two-stage stratified cluster sample design: schools are sampled first (with PPS selection within strata) and classrooms are sampled within schools; in some countries an optional third stage samples students within classrooms. It also documents within-country exclusions at the school and student levels (e.g., educable mentally disabled students, functionally disabled students, and non-native-language speakers who cannot overcome the language barrier), and notes that exclusions should be limited to no more than 10% of national desired populations. For performance assessment, it specifies subsampling rules from the written assessment sample (e.g., sampling at least 50 schools and 9 or 18 upper-grade students per school) and allows additional exclusions for quality/administration constraints.

data.outcome_summary: This document is a user guide for the TIMSS International Database (Primary and Middle School Years), covering data collected in 1995 for TIMSS Populations 1 and 2. It explains the database contents (achievement scores from written and performance assessments, background questionnaires for students/teachers/schools, sampling weights, and codebooks) and the underlying sampling design (two-stage stratified cluster sampling with optional student subsampling). It describes TIMSS scaling and achievement-score construction using IRT-based models and the plausible values framework: five plausible values are drawn per student and transformed to an international scale (mean 500, SD 100), with the international reports using only the first plausible value for reporting. It also documents how to compute sampling variance using jackknife repeated replication (JRR) and how to use different weight variants (TOTWGT, SENWGT, HOUWGT) depending on whether analysts want population estimates, equal country contribution, or sample-size-based significance testing. No predictive ML results are reported because the guide is methodological documentation rather than an empirical modeling study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a technical database user guide rather than an empirical research paper. As such, it does not define a predictive target variable, does not train or compare ML models, and does not report model performance metrics or effects. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, main findings, and conceptual predictors are intentionally empty, while survey design and plausible-values/scaling documentation are provided to support secondary analysts.
